No /usr/bin/time. Use bash `time` keyword or `date`. Let me rewrite using bash's built-in time and also measure with `SECONDS`. Simpler: use `time` shell keyword.

Also note: the "BIG OUT OK" is bogus because all files were empty. Let me fix.

arguments.command:
cat > /work/tmp/big.sh <<'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
set -u
BIN=/work/submit/planb64
T=/work/tmp
seed=$1; nfib=$2; ntr=$3
python3 $T/gen.py $seed $nfib $ntr $T/bfib.txt $T/btrace.txt
echo "--- build cpp"; time $BIN build $T/bfib.txt $T/bgot.idx
echo "--- build ref"; time python3 $T/ref.py build $T/bfib.txt > $T/bref.idx
cmp $T/bgot.idx $T/bref.idx && echo "BIG IDX OK ($nfib)"
for m in scalar "batch 256" "batch 007"; do
  echo "--- lookup $m"; time $BIN lookup $T/bgot.idx $T/btrace.txt $m > $T/bgot.$$.out
  cp $T/bgot.$$.out $T/bgot_$(echo $m | tr ' ' '_').out
  rm -f $T/bgot.$$.out
done
echo "--- lookup ref"; time python3 $T/ref.py lookup $T/bref.idx $T/btrace.txt > $T/bref.out
cmp $T/bgot_scalar.out $T/bref.out && cmp $T/bgot_batch_256.out $T/bref.out && cmp $T/bgot_batch_007.out $T/bref.out && echo "BIG OUT OK ($ntr)"
wc -l $T/bfib.txt $T/btrace.txt $T/bgot.idx
EOF
chmod +x /work/tmp/big.sh
cd /work/tmp && ./big.sh 777 5000 20000 2>&1 | tail -40
